newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner H1 profits up, below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner H1 profits up, below forecasts.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA on Tuesday reported a strong recovery in first-half profits.

Kvaerner, which has its headquarters in London but is listed on the Oslo stock exchange, said pre-tax profit rose 19 percent to 840 million Norwegian crowns, while operating profits jumped 73 percent to 963 million.
However, the results failed to meet the expectations of analysts, who were looking for operating profit of around 1.2 billion crowns.
Group sales rose sharply, largely reflecting the contribution of Britain's Trafalgar House group of companies bought in April 1996 for $1.37 billion.

Kvaerner president and chief executive officer Erik Tonseth repeated his forecast of "much better operating profit" for 1997 as a whole, but said while underlying trading was improving it was "still not satisfactory".

Orders in the first half were sharply higher, totalling 51 billion crowns compared with 17 billion a year before. Pre-tax profits in shipbuilding, Kvaerner's main money-making operation, slipped slightly to 525 million crowns from 545 million, while construction lost 39 million crowns. Kvaerner predicted "a good result" for shipbuilding in 1997, and said the troubled construction division should break even.
Results in the languishing pulp and paper business continued to pick up, with losses for the half year narrowing to 27 million crowns from 133 million.
